governing_rule: No IA may be omitted because its high-level body is reducible. Every one of the 60 frozen IA identities has an exact native primitive body.

admitted.title: source quotient cannot reconstruct distinguished exact residual bits

admitted.title: scalar Boolean consistency is not forced by XOR syntax alone
admitted.body: The represented Boolean XOR relation admits the concrete 4x4 reconvergence constraint system while the concrete 5x4 obstruction constraint system is inconsistent; scalar consistency depends on the represented incidence/delta constraints rather than following from XOR syntax alone.

admitted.title: binary-tie XOR law does not imply continuation-phase integrability
admitted.body: The exact binary-tie relation BINARY_TIE_ALLOWED iff XOR-zero and the exact 5x4 scalar-continuation obstruction coexist in the represented system; therefore binary-tie XOR exactness alone does not imply scalar continuation-phase integrability.
admitted.scope: represented binary-tie layer versus represented 5x4 continuation layer

admitted.title: residual incidence supplies an intrinsic discriminator absent from the current quotient on the witness
admitted.body: There exists represented residual-membership structure that distinguishes fine members of both the source and target quotient nodes in the shortest 5x4 obstruction.

admitted.title: coarse endpoints are insufficient to reconstruct observed transition orientation/history
admitted.body: The current ordered coarse endpoint pair is insufficient to reconstruct either the observed accumulated full-transporter mapping or the observed ordered source-frame action sequence on the shortest 5x4 routes.

admitted.title: shortest obstruction forces a model change
admitted.body: Within one-Boolean-value-per-current-quotient-node semantics, no exact successor model can simultaneously preserve both shortest 5x4 routes, their current shared source/target quotient identifications, and all four current edge-delta constraints while making the phase path-independent. At least one of those load-bearing conditions must change.
admitted.scope: shortest 5x4 obstruction under scalar Boolean node-potential semantics

admitted.title: state-refinement-only repair must break a shared endpoint identification
admitted.body: If the two shortest 5x4 routes, their four edge deltas, and one Boolean value per refined node are retained unchanged, any repair achieved solely by state refinement must separate at least one currently shared route endpoint occurrence; retaining both current shared endpoint identifications reproduces the inconsistent constraint system.
admitted.scope: shortest 5x4 obstruction; conditional on state-refinement-only repair

admitted.title: unchanged quotient and deltas force departure from scalar node-potential semantics
admitted.body: If both current shared quotient endpoint identifications and all four shortest-witness edge deltas are retained, the witness cannot be made path-independent by assigning one Boolean phase value to each current quotient node; a successful correction must instead change the phase codomain/edge semantics, refine the quotient, remove an asserted route/edge, or abandon scalar path-independence.

admitted.title: an erased residual distinction lies directly on the obstructed quotient seam
admitted.body: The shortest 5x4 scalar obstruction occurs across quotient nodes that merge represented fine states with residual-membership differences; therefore an exact fine residual distinction is present at the same quotient seam where scalar path consistency fails.

admitted.title: continuation obstruction does not falsify the binary-tie XOR layer
admitted.body: The represented 5x4 scalar continuation obstruction and the represented binary-tie XOR-zero equivalence are jointly satisfiable because they constrain distinct predicates/carriers; the continuation counterexample does not negate the exact binary-tie relation.
admitted.scope: packet-local scope separation between continuation and binary-tie layers

admitted.title: one represented target residual bit defines a strict local refinement
admitted.body: Within target quotient node 197002, the predicate 'P0 residual token 197700 has membership bit 1' separates final state 197403 from final state 197402, so adjoining that represented bit to target identity strictly refines this quotient fiber.
admitted.scope: target fiber of shortest 5x4 obstruction only

admitted.title: the residual-bit target refinement repairs the shortest scalar constraint system
admitted.body: Keep the four shortest-witness edge deltas and one Boolean phase value per refined node, but replace the merged target by two refined targets distinguished by the represented 197700 membership bit. The resulting constraints are satisfiable; exactly two Boolean assignments exist, related by simultaneous complement.
admitted.scope: shortest 5x4 obstruction only; refined target split by represented residual membership

admitted.title: full transporter history is not necessary for local repair of the shortest obstruction
admitted.body: The shortest 5x4 scalar contradiction can be removed while retaining the scalar Boolean codomain and all four edge deltas by refining the target with represented residual-state information; carrying the full accumulated transporter is therefore not necessary to repair this one witness.

admitted.title: coarse target identification changes scalar constraint satisfiability
admitted.body: For the shortest 5x4 witness with unchanged four edge deltas, identifying the two residual-distinct final targets as one quotient node yields an unsatisfiable one-bit node-potential system, while retaining them as two targets distinguished by the represented residual bit yields a satisfiable system.

admitted.title: quotient-level scalar obstruction does not imply obstruction on every refinement
admitted.body: The shortest 5x4 witness is an explicit model in which scalar Boolean node-potential semantics fails on the current coarse quotient but succeeds on a represented strict refinement; therefore quotient-level scalar obstruction alone does not imply scalar obstruction on every finer state carrier.
admitted.scope: logical non-implication witnessed by the shortest 5x4 obstruction/refinement pair

admitted.title: a history-free state-local repair exists for the shortest witness
admitted.body: There exists a repair of the shortest scalar contradiction that uses only represented endpoint residual-state information to refine the target and does not require accumulated transporter mapping content or ordered source-frame action sequence as part of refined node content.

admitted.title: the shortest obstruction is a quotient-sensitive rather than quotient-invariant fact
admitted.body: Whether the shortest 5x4 edge observations admit a scalar Boolean node potential depends on the declared state-identification relation: the answer is false under the current target merge and true under the represented residual-bit target refinement.
admitted.scope: shortest 5x4 witness under the two explicitly represented state-identification relations

admitted.title: shortest-route phase equals the distinguished final residual bit
admitted.body: For each of the two shortest 5x4 routes, the observed route phase bit equals the P0 membership bit of residual token 197700 in that route's represented final exact residual state: route A gives 0=0 and route B gives 1=1.
admitted.scope: exactly the two shortest 5x4 routes represented in the packet

admitted.title: required target phase difference equals residual-bit difference
admitted.body: In every satisfying scalar assignment of the residual-bit-refined shortest witness, the two refined target phase values differ by XOR 1, and the two represented target residual-membership bits also differ by XOR 1.

admitted.title: the coarse target merge identifies values forced to differ
admitted.body: The current target quotient merge identifies the two final states even though every satisfying refinement-level scalar assignment requires their target phase values to differ; imposing one shared target phase value is therefore exactly the additional equality that makes the shortest constraint system inconsistent.

admitted.title: a local endpoint residual coordinate reproduces route phase
admitted.body: On the represented two-route shortest-witness family, after refining the target by residual-token-197700 membership, route phase is an endpoint function of that refined residual bit; no route-history variable is needed to distinguish phase 0 from phase 1 for these two routes.

admitted.title: current target quotient erases a locally phase-determining endpoint coordinate
admitted.body: On the shortest two-route family, target residual-token-197700 membership determines the observed route phase, yet the current target quotient merges the two final states with opposite values of that bit.

admitted.title: target-only state refinement is sufficient for local satisfiability
admitted.body: For the shortest 5x4 witness, the source quotient node and both intermediate nodes may remain unchanged; splitting only the merged target by residual-token-197700 membership is sufficient to make the scalar Boolean edge equations satisfiable.

admitted.title: refined shortest witness has exactly global-complement gauge freedom
admitted.body: The residual-bit-refined shortest-witness constraint system has exactly two Boolean node assignments, and one is obtained from the other by complementing every node phase bit.

admitted.title: fixing source phase uniquely fixes the refined shortest witness
admitted.body: In the residual-bit-refined shortest system, choosing the source node phase bit fixes every intermediate and target phase bit uniquely.

admitted.title: refined target potential equals source potential XOR residual bit
admitted.body: For each shortest route in every satisfying refined assignment, target_phase = source_phase XOR final_P0_residual_197700_membership.

admitted.title: final residual bit is an exact local phase correction term
admitted.body: For both shortest routes, observed_route_phase XOR final_P0_residual_197700_membership = 0.

admitted.title: endpoint residual correction flattens the shortest route pair
admitted.body: Define corrected_route_bit = observed_route_phase XOR final_P0_residual_197700_membership for the two shortest routes. The corrected bit is 0 on both routes.

admitted.title: the shortest obstruction alone does not force a larger phase codomain
admitted.body: Because the shortest 5x4 contradiction is satisfiable after a strict state refinement while retaining one Boolean phase value per refined node and retaining all four edge deltas, this witness alone does not establish that a higher-dimensional, non-binary, or non-abelian phase codomain is necessary.

admitted.title: two refined target identities are locally necessary and sufficient
admitted.body: Any state-refinement-only scalar repair of the shortest witness must place final states 197402 and 197403 in distinct refined target identities, and the represented residual-bit split provides exactly such two distinct target identities with a satisfying scalar assignment.

admitted.title: concrete 4x4 flat witness has exactly two complement-related assignments
admitted.body: The six-node concrete 4x4 zero-delta reconvergence system has exactly two Boolean node-potential assignments: all nodes 0 and all nodes 1.

admitted.title: fixing the 4x4 source phase uniquely fixes the concrete flat witness
admitted.body: In the explicit 4x4 two-route witness, fixing the source node phase uniquely fixes every other represented node phase.

admitted.body: Both the explicit flat 4x4 witness and the residual-bit-refined shortest 5x4 witness have exactly two satisfying scalar assignments related by global complement; the local residual refinement removes the contradiction without introducing additional absolute phase choices in that witness.
admitted.scope: comparison of the two explicitly primitive-supported finite constraint systems

admitted.title: relative endpoint phase equals the distinguished residual bit
admitted.body: For each shortest route in every satisfying residual-bit-refined assignment, target_phase XOR source_phase equals the final P0 residual-token-197700 membership bit.

admitted.title: the local residual correction is independent of absolute phase gauge
admitted.body: Simultaneously complementing source and target phase bits leaves target_phase XOR source_phase unchanged; therefore the equality in SC-IA048 is invariant under the only global-complement gauge freedom of the refined shortest witness.

admitted.title: the corrected local relation survives observed transporter/history difference
admitted.body: The two shortest routes have different full-transporter mappings and different ordered source-frame action sequences, yet both satisfy the same gauge-invariant relation target_phase XOR source_phase = final residual-token-197700 membership; those represented transition/history differences do not prevent this state-local relative relation on the two-route family.

admitted.title: source residual refinement is not necessary for the shortest local scalar repair
admitted.body: Although source quotient node 197000 merges represented residual-distinct fine sheets, the shortest scalar constraint system is satisfiable after splitting only the target while leaving source quotient node 197000 unchanged; source-sheet residual refinement is therefore not necessary for this local repair.

admitted.title: shortest-witness state-refinement repair is target-asymmetric
admitted.body: Under unchanged routes, edge deltas, and scalar Boolean codomain, every state-refinement-only repair of the shortest witness must separate the two fine target states, while at least one satisfying repair leaves the represented source merge unchanged.

admitted.title: route-A transporter is an odd involution
admitted.body: The complete mapping 197500 fixes slots 0,1,4 and swaps slots 2 and 3; applying it twice returns every represented slot to itself, and its inversion parity is 1.

admitted.title: route-B transporter is an odd involution
admitted.body: The complete mapping 197501 fixes slots 2,3,4 and swaps slots 0 and 1; applying it twice returns every represented slot to itself, and its inversion parity is 1.

admitted.title: relative transporter is even
admitted.body: The definitionally composed transporter 197502 = 197501 after 197500 maps slots as [1,0,3,2,4], has exactly two inversions, and therefore has represented parity bit 0.

admitted.title: route phase difference is odd while relative transporter parity is even
admitted.body: The two shortest route phases differ by XOR 1, while the exact relative transporter 197502 has parity bit 0.

admitted.title: relative transporter parity cannot explain the shortest phase difference
admitted.body: On the shortest 5x4 two-route witness, even relative transporter parity coexists with an odd route-phase difference; relative transporter parity alone therefore cannot equal or determine the represented phase difference on this pair.

admitted.title: oriented action histories share their second action and differ at the first
admitted.body: The two represented source-frame action sequences are (1,2) and (0,2): their second action slot is the same represented slot 2 and their first action slots differ.

admitted.title: relative transporter is an even involution with two disjoint swaps
admitted.body: The definitionally composed relative transporter 197502 swaps slots 0 and 1, swaps slots 2 and 3, fixes slot 4, and applying it twice returns every represented slot to itself; its represented parity bit is 0.

admitted.title: absolute sign plus common second action does not determine route phase
admitted.body: The two shortest routes both have accumulated transporter-sign bit 1 and the same second source-frame action slot 2, yet their computed route-phase bits are 0 and 1; the pair (absolute sign, second action) does not determine route phase on this witness.
